signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention Risk + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 160.09, breaching the 160.00 psychological handle that previously triggered Japanese authorities to act. BoJ Governor Ueda reportedly met US Treasury Secretary Bessent on Sunday, a high-level engagement that intensifies market scrutiny of coordinated policy action as the pair tests new highs. While a 267bp SOFR-TONA carry advantage structurally favors the USD, the options market is aggressively pricing downside protection, evidenced by a strong USD/JPY 25d risk reversal of -1.74. This divergence between spot momentum and institutional hedging suggests a crowded carry trade vulnerable to a policy-induced shock. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; 160.00 level invites intervention risk. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias remains. Risk: Lack of imminent BoJ/MoF action allows carry-driven momentum to extend toward 162.00.

signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + RBNZ
signals.text: The USD/NZD spread has expanded to 1.117% over the past week, marking a dominant bilateral theme as the USD outperforms (+0.580%) and the NZD lags (-0.537%) across G10 peers. NZD/USD trades at 0.5897, currently testing its SMA20 at 0.5912 as spec positioning hits a 52-week extreme with a COT LF net short pctl of 0 and z-score of -2.60. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. A 125bp SOFR-OCR carry advantage for the USD supports the current trend, but the extreme spec positioning leaves the pair highly sensitive to any NZD data beats. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD; G10 divergence and carry favor USD. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike bias priced. Risk: RBNZ hike triggers a short-squeeze in the crowded spec net-short position.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Real Rates
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3535, holding just below its SMA20 at 1.3546. The options market is pricing an extreme volatility risk premium, with 1M ATM IV at 11.0% vs a realized HV30 of 4.9%, a 6.1-point spread that reflects significant hedging demand ahead of September policy meetings. While the BoE-Fed nominal spread is neutral at 0bp, the real policy rate differential favors the USD (+1.45%) over the GBP (+0.35%) due to higher UK inflation expectations. COT data shows specs are heavily long GBP (pctl 96, z +1.58), suggesting a 'crowded long' setup that is failing to push price above moving average resistance. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD; crowded long positioning meets negative real rate differential. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep. Risk: Fed shifts to a neutral bias, narrowing the real rate gap and relieving pressure on Cable.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Retail vs Institutional Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7148, remaining above its SMA20/50/200 cluster despite a 1W decline of 0.65%. A significant sentiment divergence has emerged, as retail traders are 88% short (an extreme contrarian signal) while institutional COT LF positioning remains heavily net long at +53,578 (pctl 95, z +1.92). The 70bp AONIA-SOFR carry premium continues to support the AUD, and with an RBA hold expected, the institutional bias remains focused on the yield advantage. However, the lack of further WoW adds to the COT long position suggests the bullish move is losing momentum. Trade bias: Neutral/Bullish AUD/USD; retail extreme short provides a contrarian floor. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep. Risk: A sharp drop in iron ore or copper prices invalidates the institutional long thesis.
